claims.text: Mg-Ti-Zn alloys can be synthesized by mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering.
The initial MgTiZn material is a metastable, single-phase solid solution.
Thermal exposure of the metastable alloy induces a discontinuous precipitation reaction.
MgTiZn alloys can contain Ti2Zn and Mg21Zn25 intermetallic phases.
Exposure near 350°C produces a fine, homogeneous dispersion of nanoscale intermetallic precipitates.
Exposure near 500°C accelerates precipitate coarsening and promotes intergranular segregation.
Uniformly distributed fine intermetallics in MgTiZn promote formation of a protective surface film and passivation.
The protective surface film on MgTiZn is TiO2-rich.
The fine precipitate population produced near 350°C maintains or slightly improves corrosion resistance relative to the metastable baseline.
The fine precipitate population produced near 350°C maintains or slightly improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Coarse, grain-boundary-associated intermetallics disrupt the continuity of the protective oxide film.
Intermetallic morphology, size, and spatial distribution can affect corrosion behavior through shielding or micro-galvanic effects.
The 500°C-treated material will have a higher corrosion current density than both the 350°C-treated material and the baseline.
The 500°C-treated material will have poorer high-temperature oxidation resistance than the 350°C-treated material and the baseline.
Approximately 350°C and 500°C define distinct service-regime boundaries for passivation retention and degradation, respectively.
The water-quenched reference is a metastable, single-phase solid-solution state.
Mg-containing Mg-Ti-Zn alloys have a tendency to develop intermetallic compounds rather than remain wholly single phase.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis associates thermal treatment with development of a TiO2-rich film and proposes time-resolved XPS during that exposure, while the stated thermal treatments occur under an inert atmosphere specifically to avoid extraneous oxidation. It is therefore unclear whether the relevant film forms during treatment, during subsequent air exposure, or during the corrosion/oxidation test.

The initial state is described as arising from mechanical alloying and rapid consolidation, whereas the reference is described as water-quenched; the relationship between these preparation histories is not specified, so it is unclear whether they are actually the same initial state.
